label: Nuisance Parameters and the Neyman-Scott Problem
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 191 through 213 and asks what happens when the parameter we care about is entangled with many nuisance directions. The Neyman-Scott setting is the warning case: every new group adds a fresh nuisance mean, so the fiber dimension grows alongside the sample and ordinary likelihood intuition quietly breaks.

label: Nuisance Fibers Over a Target
notes: Write the model as a target coordinate psi and a nuisance coordinate lambda. Fixing psi leaves a fiber of nuisance values, and the manifold becomes a bundle of such fibers. Classical asymptotics assume the fiber dimension is fixed while data grow; the incidental-parameter regime violates that assumption directly.

label: The Neyman-Scott Variance Experiment
notes: With two observations per group and one mean per group, the profile likelihood variance estimator converges to half the truth no matter how many groups we collect. The simulation confirms the persistent bias: concentrating around the wrong value is worse than being noisy, because more data buys false confidence.

label: Incidental-Parameter Inconsistency
notes: The bias is structural, not a small-sample wrinkle. Each group mean consumes one degree of freedom, so dividing the residual sum by group size m instead of m minus one shrinks the estimate by the factor m minus one over m. Dividing by n times m minus one restores consistency.

label: Estimating Functions
notes: An estimating function G is unbiased when its expectation vanishes at the true target value for every nuisance value. Solving G equals zero defines an estimator without committing to a full likelihood. The right G encodes orthogonality to nuisance motion and the correct degrees-of-freedom accounting, which is exactly what the profile likelihood missed.

label: The Nuisance Tangent Space and Efficient Score
notes: The naive target score leans partly into nuisance directions. Project it onto the nuisance tangent space and subtract: the residual is the efficient score, orthogonal to every nuisance direction. The Pythagorean split of squared norms verifies the decomposition, and orthogonality is the geometric definition of efficiency.

label: Semiparametric Projection
notes: In a semiparametric model the nuisance object can be a whole function: a baseline density, a censoring law, a firing-rate background. The efficient score is still a projection, now in an L-squared inner product. We approximate the infinite nuisance space by a finite basis, project the target score, and keep the residual.

label: Spike Intervals as a Local Diagnostic
notes: The nuisance theme reappears in point processes. A rate background is nuisance; a stimulus modulation is the target. Inter-spike intervals shorten where the background rate rises, so local bursts can mimic target signal. The diagnostic warns that bursts must be separated by an estimating rule, not admired by the raw likelihood.

label: What the Geometry Teaches
notes: The lesson is not that likelihood is bad but that its geometry must be inspected when nuisance dimension changes with sample size. Estimating functions and semiparametric projection answer one question: which variation is genuinely informative about the target after nuisance motion has been removed? Replication and within-group centering are the practical repairs.
